intent: To demonstrate the increasing trend of reported rape cases in India from 2008 to 2016.

units.meaning: Reported rape cases in India trend upward over 2008–2016, from 19,923.404 in 2008 to 37,923.404 in 2016.
accepted_routes: Reported rape cases generally increased from 2008 to 2016.
The series rises overall from about 19,900 in 2008 to about 37,900 in 2016.
There is an upward trend across the period, despite year-to-year variation.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A line/bar series for 2008–2016 must visibly ascend overall; the start and end years should be identifiable.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration clause stating that reported rape cases have been increasing
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show an overall upward trend across the full 2008–2016 period, even if it does not annotate every year?

units.meaning: The 2016 endpoint is the maximum shown: 37,923.404 reported cases, higher than all earlier years.

basis.note: final and highest year in the series

accepted_routes: In 2016, reported rape cases reached about 37,900.
The final year, 2016, ends at 37,923.404 cases.
2016 is the highest year shown, at roughly 37,900 reported cases.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2016 bar/point must be labeled or clearly end the series at its highest level.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration phrase 'from 2008 to 2016' or the end of the increasing-trend statement
units.reviewer_question: Must the 2016 endpoint value, and/or its status as the highest year, be explicitly conveyed?

units.meaning: The largest year-over-year rise is 2012 to 2013: 23,923.404 to 31,923.404, an increase of 8,000 cases.

basis.note: year before the largest annual jump
year after the largest annual jump

accepted_routes: The biggest single-year jump is from 2012 to 2013, up about 8,000 cases.
Reported cases rise most sharply between 2012 and 2013, from roughly 23,900 to 31,900.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Adjacent 2012 and 2013 bars/points must show the largest vertical increase, ideally with the difference annotated.
units.temporal_anchor: optional callout during the overall increasing-trend narration
units.reviewer_question: Is the largest year-over-year increase optional, or should the video single it out?

units.meaning: The series is not monotonic: reported cases fall from 34,927.660 in 2014 to 32,927.660 in 2015, a decrease of 2,000.
accepted_routes: There is a dip in 2015, down about 2,000 from 2014.
Reported cases decline from roughly 34,900 in 2014 to 32,900 in 2015.
2014 to 2015 is a year-over-year decrease of 2,000 cases.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2015 bar/point must be visibly lower than 2014, and the decline may be labeled.
units.temporal_anchor: optional qualification within or after the increasing-trend narration
units.reviewer_question: Must the video acknowledge the 2015 decline to avoid implying a strictly monotonic rise?

units.meaning: Apart from 2016, 2014 is the second-highest year shown, above 2015 and 2013; 2016 is 2,995.744 cases higher than 2014 and 4,995.744 higher than 2015.
accepted_routes: The top three years are 2016, 2014, then 2015.
2016 exceeds 2014 by about 3,000 and 2015 by about 5,000 cases.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Bars/points for 2014, 2015, and 2016 must allow the ranking 2016 > 2014 > 2015 to be read.
units.temporal_anchor: optional ranking/comparison callout near the later years
units.reviewer_question: Should the video show late-period ranking/comparison, or is endpoint change alone sufficient?

optional_valid: 2008 and 2009 are equal at 19,923.404 reported cases.
The total increase from 2008 to 2016 is 18,000 cases, about +90.3%.
2015 is lower than 2014 but still higher than 2013.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not claim actual rape incidence increased; the data are reported cases only.
Do not claim every year rose monotonically; 2015 declined.
Do not extrapolate beyond 2016 or infer causes.
Do not use per-capita/population-normalized rates or denominators not in the table.
Do not use arbitrary thresholds or values not derivable from the table.
notes: The core required content is the overall upward trend and the 2008-to-2016 endpoint; the largest jump and 2015 dip are useful optional nuance. Keep all figures tied to the table and avoid causal or normalized-rate claims.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
